extracted.intended_audience: developers contributing code, tests, documentation, or packaging to the SageMath project (Sage) via GitHub
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and standards for developing, testing, documenting, packaging, and submitting changes to the SageMath codebase, using Git/GitHub, doctests, documentation builds, and distribution packaging. Covers workflows for issues, pull requests, reviews, and modularized distribution testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commit message format
rubrics_metrics.description: The commit message should generally have a one-line description, followed by an empty line, followed by further explanatory text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Example:
Added the last twin prime

This is an example commit message. You see there is a one-line summary followed by more detailed description, if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a branch per work item
rubrics_metrics.description: Work on a new branch based on develop; do not work directly on develop or master.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create branch with git checkout -b my_branch develop. Branches are local unless pushed; push to your fork (origin) when ready: git push origin my_branch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing changes before PR
rubrics_metrics.description: Every change of Sage source code must be tested before being merged; testing is highly valued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run doctests for modified files: ./sage -t path/to/your/file.py. Restart Sage to pick up Python/Cython changes. Ensure tests pass and add doctests where appropriate. See Running Sage’s Doctests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctest requirement for bug fixes
rubrics_metrics.description: Every bug fixed should result in a doctest illustrating that the bug has been fixed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The new doctest should contain the issue or PR number, e.g. See :issue:12345.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pull request creation and content
rubrics_metrics.description: PRs should have a concise title and a body explaining what the PR does; if it solves an issue, describe that and add links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use gh pr create or the web UI. Add type/component/priority labels. Use '- Depends on' lines for dependencies. If not ready for review, open as draft.

rubrics_metrics.name: PR status labels and meanings
rubrics_metrics.description: Use status labels with prefix s: to indicate PR lifecycle state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: s: needs review — ready for peer review; s: needs work — changes required; s: needs info — author should provide more info; s: positive review — merged in due time. Use resolution labels r: duplicate, r: invalid, r: wontfix, r: worksforme when closing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checks required for PR merges
rubrics_metrics.description: All automated checks should pass before merging: lint, build & test, documentation build, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linting with pycodestyle and Relint; GitHub Actions build/test workflow builds Sage incrementally and runs tests; documentation build workflow builds HTML/PDF and posts preview links. Inspect workflow runs for failures and address them before requesting review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must check code purpose, documentation, tests, conventions, and potential regressions before approving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: Does code address PR's aim? Any new problems? User documentation clear? Code documentation sufficient? Conventions (Sage/Python/Cython) followed? Doctest coverage adequate? Bugfix doctests present? Speedup claims tested? Manuals build? Run full tests including long doctests and optional tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to comment (issue vs PR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments about reported issues should go on the issue; comments about submitted code should go on the PR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a PR is linked to an issue and it's unclear where to post, follow above rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bug report contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A bug report should contain an explicit reproducible example, expected behavior, version info, and platform details where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include Sage version and versions of optional packages, OS and CPU architecture if relevant. Provide URLs or sage-devel discussion references if useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning an enhancement / opening issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Before opening an issue for an enhancement, search for existing issues/PRs and discuss on sage-devel if unsure; open specific issues rather than broad ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be precise in titles (mention OS if relevant). Avoid vague/unmeasurable goals. Provide background URLs and label appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue labeling conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use labels with prefixes to classify issues: type t:, component c:, priority p:, and wishlist if not urgent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: t: bug, t: enhancement; c: linear algebra; p: minor / 4, p: blocker / 1. Use labels to make triage effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stopgap procedure for dangerous regressions
rubrics_metrics.description: When Sage returns wrong results, create a stopgap issue and a stopgap PR that adds a warning until a fix is available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sage.misc.stopgap.stopgap("message", ISSUE_NUM) in code to warn users. Stopgap items should be marked critical. Do not use stopgap when Sage crashes for mathematically valid code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation previews and checks
rubrics_metrics.description: PRs get HTML documentation previews and PDF builds; authors should check documentation previews and PDF builds succeed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HTML preview published at doc-pr-<PR>-sagemath.netlify.app; a changes log is generated. PDF docs built by PDF workflow—author should ensure PDF build passed before requesting review. The HTML preview includes TESTS blocks for PR checks; final release docs do not include TESTS blocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build manuals and check formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: When changing code/documentation, ensure the reference manual builds without errors and the output looks correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check both HTML and PDF builds; inspect formatting and hyperlinks for typos or broken links introduced by changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctests: writing testable examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Doctests should be present for functions and methods and should exercise relevant behavior; doctests are central to Sage's testing culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sage -coverage <files> to check coverage. Mark doctests with # optional or # needs when depending on optional features. Make doctests suitable for modularized testing by conditionalizing on features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctest tags and feature mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: Use doctest tags like # optional and # needs with feature names (e.g., sage.symbolic) to express conditional doctest dependencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: # needs is conventionally used for features present in a standard install. Feature names should hide implementation details (e.g., use sage.rings.finite_rings rather than sage.libs.pari). sage –fixdoctests rewrites tags according to convention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaring optional and doctest-only dependencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional run-time dependencies and doctest-only dependencies should be declared via extras_require in setup.cfg (generated from setup.cfg.m4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows users to install extras like pip install sagemath-coding[symbolics]. extras_require does not affect build phase but provides nicknames for add-on installs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Runtime dependency policy for optional functionality
rubrics_metrics.description: If a method provides core functionality, declare its runtime dependency; if it only provides optional features, do not declare the heavy dependency and leave it to the user.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether symbolic or heavy dependencies should be installed automatically or provided as extras. Use features mapping to provide installation hints to users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packaging: hierarchy and modularized distributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Sage is split into distribution packages with a hierarchy indicating install_requires (solid arrows) and extras_require (dashed arrows).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: sagemath-objects, sagemath-categories, sagemath-repl, sagemath-standard, sagemath-standard-no-symbolics. Understand package graph before adding dependencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing modularized distribution packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution packages must be testable separately using virtual environments (tox), while still enabling integration testing with other parts of Sage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build wheels with make wheels, then create tox virtual envs to install wheels and run tests. Use SAGE_VENV/var/lib/sage/wheels for wheel files. Use tox.ini in each pkgs/* distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing distributions without full Sage (small distributions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Small distributions (e.g., sagemath-objects) should be installable and testable without requiring the full Sage wheels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tox to create virtual envs using PyPI dependencies and run tests; recognize current limitations where doctests rely on higher-level bits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Conda-based editable builds for development
rubrics_metrics.description: Developers are recommended to use Conda environments and install Sage editable into them for development convenience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create and activate env: conda env create --file environment-3.12-linux.yml --name sage-dev; conda activate sage-dev; pip install --no-build-isolation --editable . ; start Sage with sage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Git/GitHub workflow and remotes setup
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a fork-on-GitHub workflow: fork sagemath/sage, clone your fork, add upstream remote, and avoid pushing to upstream by mistake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set origin to your fork and upstream to sagemath/sage. Optional: disable upstream pushes: git remote set-url --push upstream DISABLE. Use origin and upstream naming conventions. Commands for adding remotes provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using GitHub CLI (gh)
rubrics_metrics.description: gh can be used to create/check out PRs and set defaults and extensions; authenticate via gh auth login.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authenticate with web browser or token, set default repo with gh repo set-default sagemath/sage, use gh pr create and gh pr checkout, install extensions like gh-act for local Actions testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merging upstream develop into branch and handling conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep your branch up-to-date by fetching and merging upstream develop; resolve conflicts manually when they occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fast-forward local develop: git fetch upstream develop:develop; merge into your branch with git merge develop. See Conflict resolution section for details when merge conflicts occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linting and automated style checks
rubrics_metrics.description: PRs must pass linting workflows that check code style against pycodestyle-minimal and Relint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect failing checks via GitHub Actions UI; fix style issues before requesting review. Familiarize with Sage code conventions in the Writing Code for Sage chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation: TESTS blocks in PR previews only
rubrics_metrics.description: HTML previews and PDF previews for PRs include TESTS blocks to help verify newly added TESTS; official release docs do not include TESTS blocks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use previews to check TESTS blocks for correctness; ensure tests included in documentation are appropriate for preview only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance-aware import patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid importing heavy modules at module load time or just for isinstance checks; prefer abstract base classes, lazy_import, or caching to reduce runtime costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid modularization anti-pattern of importing heavy classes just to use isinstance. Provide ABCs in light-dependency modules and use isinstance(object, abc.Class). Use lazy_import() or try/except ImportError with Pluffe = () fallback and cache failures so imports happen once, not on every call. Examples and timeit benchmarks provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid modularization anti-pattern
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not import classes from heavy-dependency modules merely to run isinstance tests or call helper functions; this creates heavy dependencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce an abstract base class (ABC) in a light-dependency module and make the heavy class subclass it; then use isinstance against the ABC. Example: use sage.rings.abc.pAdicField rather than importing pAdicFieldGeneric from heavy modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caching failed imports for performance
rubrics_metrics.description: When an import may fail (module not installed), catch ImportError once and cache a fallback (e.g., an empty tuple) to avoid repeated slow failures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example idiom: try: from xxxx import Pluffe except ImportError: Pluffe = (). This makes isinstance checks fast after the first attempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Building wheels for distribution testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Build wheels for Sage distributions to enable separate virtual environment tests of distribution packages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run make wheels or ./configure --enable-wheels to make wheels available in SAGE_VENV/var/lib/sage/wheels and use them to install into tox virtual environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual UI testing where automated tests lack coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: For changes affecting UI components (IPython, Jupyter, plotting), rely on manual testing because automated tests may not cover UI sufficiently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Jupyter notebooks with comprehensive tests of graphics and typesetting; perform manual checks alongside automated tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and PR author responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: PR authors should check documentation previews and PDF builds and ensure documentation changes are correctly reflected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A link to built doc is added in a comment on PR by the build workflow; if doc build fails, examine Actions runs and fix issues. Ensure documentation for new features is discoverable and clearly explains mathematical notions or links to explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of gh pr checkout for reviewing PRs locally
rubrics_metrics.description: Use gh pr checkout <PR number> to fetch and checkout the branch of an existing PR for local testing and review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: gh pr checkout downloads refs/pull/<PR>/head and creates a local branch so you can run tests locally and inspect changes.
